display_name: The First Schedule of the Criminal Procedure Code 2010 (tabular statement of offences under the Penal Code 1871) as a lookup, with the rules that read it: arrestable, warrant or summons, bailable, trial court (ss 2(1), 7 to 9)
scope: The First Schedule as printed in SSO's PDF, current version as at 01 Oct 2026: all 478 printed rows (chapters 3 to 23) and the four rows printed under 'Offences against laws other than the Penal Code 1871', each with its seven columns; and the provisions that read it: s 2(1) 'arrestable offence', 'non-arrestable offence', 'bailable offence' and 'fine-only offence', and ss 7 to 9 (trial courts). NOT encoded: every other section of the Code (Parts 1 to 22) and the Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Schedules, by the requester's instruction of 2026-10-01; the elements of the offences (Penal Code, sg/penal-code-1871); any other written law; the Criminal Procedure Rules.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the statute, and no independent test pass has been run. The First Schedule extraction was checked against a second extraction method (460 of 464 rows agree; the 4 differences are the second method merging adjacent rows) and against the section numbers of the layout text, not against a human reading of the printed table. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. NOTES.md section 6.

forks.F1: ss 7(1)(a), 8(1): an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life has no maximum 'term' of 5 or 10 years and is read as outside those paragraphs.
forks.F2: First Schedule derived rows: a cell that says 'according as to whether ... for the offence abetted/attempted/...' is encoded as 'As for the underlying offence' and answers only when the underlying offence's treatment is supplied; the printed words are kept in the row.
forks.F3: First Schedule column 7: a blank cell is read as 'no court besides the General Division of the High Court' (the column is headed 'besides the General Division of High Court').
forks.F4: The four rows under 'Offences against laws other than the Penal Code 1871' are printed after s 512(2) and are encoded as their own rows with the section 'Other written law', not as part of s 512(2).
forks.F5: 'May not arrest without warrant unless specifically empowered ... by the law offended against' is read as 'the police may not ordinarily arrest without warrant' (s 2(1) says 'ordinarily').
